intro: The indefinido moves on, the imperfect describes and the perfecto connects with today. Here they work together.
p.de pequeño.consejo: A woman says «de pequeña». It is used with the imperfect to talk about habits: «de pequeño iba al parque».
p.el colegio.consejo: The g sounds like a soft h: ko-LE-hyo. In many countries «la escuela» is also said.
p.el patio.consejo: In a school it is where children play. There are also patios in houses.
p.conserje.consejo: It works for men and women: «el conserje», «la conserje». The j sounds like a soft h.
p.época.consejo: The accent marks the first syllable: É-po-ca. You say «en aquella época» to talk about a past time.
p.recordar.consejo: At the start the r sounds strong. In the present the o changes to ue: «recuerdo», «recuerdas».
p.llover.consejo: It is only used in the third person: «llueve», «llovía», «llovió». The ll sounds like y.
p.reunión.consejo: The accent is on the o: rre-u-NIÓN. You say «reunión de antiguos alumnos» to meet again.
p.antiguo.consejo: Before the noun it can mean «former»: «mi antiguo colegio». The u in «gu» is pronounced.
p.he vuelto.consejo: «Volver» has an irregular participle: «vuelto». With «a» it means repeating: «he vuelto a leer».
b1.texto:
In a story, each past has a job:

- The **indefinido** moves the story forward: **Llegué a las ocho.**
- The **imperfect** describes the background, the habit, or what was in progress: **Llovía.**
- The **perfecto** links a period or an experience with today: **Esta semana he leído dos libros.**

This last choice changes by region: some people use the indefinido where others use the perfecto. The examples here follow a common contrast in Spain, not a rule for everyone.

Look for clues: **ayer, de repente** (indefinido), **antes, siempre, de pequeño** (imperfect), **esta semana, desde entonces** (perfecto).
b2.f0.texto: Have you ever gone back to your school?
b2.f1.texto: This week I have gone back for the first time.
b2.f2.texto: What was your school like when you were little?
b2.f3.texto: It had a huge courtyard with tall trees.
b2.f5.texto: It was raining when I reached the door.
b2.f6.texto: Suddenly my former teacher came out.
b2.f7.texto: Since then I have thought a lot about that time.
b4.texto:
An easy way to choose:

- Does it tell **an event** that moves the story forward? **Indefinido**: **llegué, esperé, salió**.
- Does it describe **what something was like**, **a habit**, or what **was going on**? **Imperfect**: **llovía, iba, era**.
- Does it connect with **today** or with a period that includes today? **Perfecto**: **he vuelto, he pensado**.

They can live in the same sentence: **Llovía cuando llegué.** (background + event)

Remember that the perfecto and the indefinido are shared out differently in different regions. Both forms are understood everywhere.
b4.e0.texto: Yesterday I arrived early and waited at the door.
b4.e1.texto: When I was little, I used to go there on foot.
b4.e2.texto: This week I have gone back to my old school.
b5.titulo: The courtyard of the tall trees
b5.f0.texto: This week I have gone back to my old school after many years.
b5.f1.texto: When I was little, I went there on foot along a tree-lined street.
b5.f2.texto: That road always smelled of wet earth.
b5.f3.texto: As a child, everything seemed huge and distant to me.
b5.f4.texto: Today the same trees have seemed smaller to me.
b5.f5.texto: Yesterday I arrived early and waited next to the iron gate.
b5.f6.texto: It was raining softly on the empty courtyard.
b5.f7.texto: Suddenly my former teacher came out with a green umbrella.
b5.f8.texto: We talked for a while and remembered the last school year.
b5.f9.texto: Since then I have thought a lot about that time.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Correct: the imperfect describes the background of the scene.
b6.o1.refuerzo: It is a specific event that moves the story forward.
b6.o2.refuerzo: It connects with today; it does not describe the background.
b6.pregunta: Which sentence describes the background weather?
b7.o0.refuerzo: «Fui» tells a single trip; «cuando era pequeño» asks for a habit.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Well done! The imperfect expresses the past habit.
b7.o2.refuerzo: The perfecto connects with today, and the sentence is about childhood.
b7.pregunta: Which form of ir expresses a habit?
b8.frase: Ayer llegué temprano y esperé en la puerta
b8.traduccion: Yesterday I arrived early and waited at the door
b9.o0.refuerzo: It describes the background, not a sudden event.
b9.o1.refuerzo: It expresses a habit, not something sudden.
b9.o2.refuerzo: That's it! «De repente salió» is a single event.
b9.pregunta: Which verb tells a sudden event?
b10.o0.refuerzo: Well done: this week includes today, and in Spain it usually goes with the perfecto.
b10.o1.refuerzo: It would express a habit, and here we talk about a specific return.
b10.o2.refuerzo: It is future: the return already happened.
b10.pregunta: Which form fits «esta semana» in Spain?
b12.o0.refuerzo: Correct: the perfecto and «desde entonces» reach to today.
b12.o1.refuerzo: It describes how you thought at that moment, not up to today.
b12.pregunta: Which sentence links the past with today?
p.vuelto.consejo: With «haber» it is «ha vuelto», the participle of «volver».
p.pensado.consejo: With «haber»: «he pensado» means I have thought.
p.esperé.consejo: The accent marks the past for yo: «espero» is now.
p.parecía.consejo: The accent on í breaks the vowels: pa-re-THÍ-a.
p.mismos.consejo: It agrees with the plural «árboles», so it ends in -os.
p.vacío.consejo: The accent on í breaks the vowels: ba-THÍ-o.
p.recordamos.consejo: The stress is on the -DA- syllable: re-kor-DA-mos.
